resourcesBrowser.newTableDescription: Define columns, keys, and constraints visually.
resourcesBrowser.newCustomDescription: Write raw SQL - CREATE VIEW, FUNCTION, or anything else.
resourcesBrowser.bulkFailed: {n} failed - selection kept so you can retry.
resourcesBrowser.selectPage: Select every row on this page
resourcesBrowser.exposeIntro: Which HTTP methods are available for {name} under the TotalBase Data API — a hard ceiling below role permissions, a method left unchecked never exists here, no matter who's asking. Uncheck all to hide this resource entirely.
resourcesBrowser.noActivity: No activity recorded for this resource yet
resourcesBrowser.dropIntro: This permanently deletes the following from PostgreSQL. This cannot be undone.

tableColumnFields.title: Title
tableColumnFields.linkHelp: Shows the value as a link to open it.
tableColumnFields.emptyTextHelp: Shown when it has no value.
tableColumnFields.colorPerRowHelp: A palette color from its row, over Color - {example}.

tableColumnsEditor.runQuery: Run the query to list its columns.

tableDrawer.blockConcurrent: Runs separately (CONCURRENTLY - can't join a transaction)
tableDrawer.previewError: Could not build the SQL statements.
tableDrawer.editDescription: Columns, indexes, and constraints - changes run as ALTER statements you confirm before they execute.
tableDrawer.checkHelp: A SQL boolean expression, for example: {example}
tableDrawer.defaultHelp: Default is a SQL expression, for example: {example1} or {example2}.
tableDrawer.concurrentlyHelp: Avoids locking the table for writes; runs outside the main transaction
tableDrawer.noIndexes: No indexes yet besides the primary key
tableDrawer.indexesHelp: A new index's name is generated when left empty. WHERE makes it a partial index, for example: {example}.
tableDrawer.readOnlyDescription: This shows existing rows - TotalBase isn't a data editor. Use the Data API or your own tools to write data.
tableDrawer.confirmIntro: This is the exact SQL that will run. Review it, then confirm.

sqlConsolePanel.purgeHelp: Deletes every history entry (from any admin) recorded before this date. The same cleanup also runs automatically on a schedule - adjust how long entries are kept in {settings}.
sqlConsolePanel.planEmpty: Run Explain to see a query plan here.

sqlConsoleDrawer.editDescription: Modify and run - this replaces the current definition (CREATE OR REPLACE).
sqlConsoleDrawer.consoleDescription: Unrestricted raw SQL - runs exactly what you type, as the configured database role. Admin-only, audited.
sqlConsoleDrawer.createDescription: Write DDL (CREATE TABLE / VIEW / FUNCTION) and run it - new resources show up in the list after refresh.

sqlResultsPanel.runPrompt: Run a statement to see results here.
sqlResultsPanel.truncated: · showing the first {shown} (Settings › SQL Console › Result row cap)

queryBuilder.buildDescription: Compose fields, filters, grouping and ordering visually - saving overwrites the JSON above.
queryBuilder.fieldsDescription: Optional - which columns to return. Empty returns every field.
queryBuilder.searchDescription: Optional full-text search term, matched across authorized text fields.
queryBuilder.whereDescription: Uses the same filter grammar as row filters and Data API where[...].
queryBuilder.groupByDescription: Optional - aggregate rows by these columns instead of returning individual records.
queryBuilder.aggregatesDescription: Only meaningful together with Group by (or alone, for a single summary row). Each row: column, function and the output name (alias).
queryBuilder.countDescription: Adds meta.count with the total matches (ignoring limit/offset) alongside data - an extra COUNT(*) query.

queryRecordsModal.summary: {total} record, with your permissions - {ms} ms. | {total} records, with your permissions - {ms} ms.

whereField.tooComplex: Current filter is too complex to build on (nested groups) - edit it directly, or clear it first.
whereField.noConditions: No conditions yet - add one above.

newTableModal.title: New table
newTableModal.kindTableDescription: Columns are added from its page afterwards.
newTableModal.kindJunctionDescription: Relates rows of two or three tables - many to many.
newTableModal.noSingleKey: {table} has no single-column primary key to point at.
newTableModal.junctionHelp: The tables it relates - each column points at its table's primary key, and a pair (or triple) appears once. Rows go when either side is deleted.
newTableModal.columnsUnique: Each column needs its own name, other than id.
newTableModal.nameJunctionDescription: Proposed from the tables it relates. For example: orders_products
newTableModal.nameDescription: Must be unique within this schema. For example: invoices
newTableModal.descriptionHelp: Optional - saved as this table's comment.
newTableModal.pkNameDescription: Column name for the primary key.
newTableModal.pkTypeDescription: UUID auto-generates a value. Serial/BigSerial auto-increment. Integer/Varchar require you to supply one.

resourceDetail.loadErrorDescription: It may have been dropped or renamed.
resourceDetail.endpointsIntro: Which HTTP methods are available for {name} under the TotalBase Data API.
resourceDetail.permanentlyDeletes: Permanently deletes {name} from PostgreSQL. This cannot be undone.
resourceDetail.dropBody: This permanently deletes {name} from PostgreSQL. This cannot be undone.

tableResourceDetail.renameHint: Renaming a table isn't supported here - use SQL Console.
tableResourceDetail.browseDataNeedsGet: Turn on GET under Endpoints to browse the data - the data browser reads through the Data API.
tableResourceDetail.endpointsIntro: Which HTTP methods are available for {name} under the TotalBase Data API — a hard ceiling below role permissions, a method turned off never exists here, no matter who's asking.

viewResourceDetail.renameHint: Renaming a view isn't supported here - use SQL Console.

functionResourceDetail.renameHint: Renaming a function isn't supported here - use SQL Console.
functionResourceDetail.classDescription: Used in this function's OpenAPI docs - QUERY for a read-like function, ACTION for one that changes data. Leave UNCLASSIFIED if unsure.
functionResourceDetail.noParameters: This function has no input parameters.

functionDetail.classDescription: Used when generating this function's OpenAPI docs - QUERY for a read-like function, ACTION for one that changes data. Leave UNCLASSIFIED if unsure.

resourceAuditing.title: Auditing
resourceAuditing.functionIntro: Every EXECUTE of {name} is always audited - there is nothing to configure.
resourceAuditing.intro: Every CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE and EXECUTE is audited: who, when, the row, and for an UPDATE the old and new value of each column it changed.
resourceAuditing.auditReadsDescription: Also write an audit entry for every READ - who asked, the fields and the filter, never the returned rows.
resourceAuditing.readsWarningTitle: Every read writes an audit entry
resourceAuditing.readsWarning: On a busy table that can be thousands a day, kept for {days}. Change it under {retention}, or see how much the log takes in {maintenance}.
resourceAuditing.excludedColumnsDescription: Never written to the log - not with the row, not in an UPDATE's changes. Password and protected columns never are anyway.
resourceAuditing.columnsUpdateError: Could not update the excluded columns

resourceColumns.title: Columns
resourceColumns.deleteDescription: This permanently drops `{name}` and all its data. This cannot be undone.
resourceColumns.brokenTitle: One reference to what is gone | {count} references to what is gone
resourceColumns.brokenDescription: These still name a column (or this table) that no longer exists - fix each where it lives.
resourceColumns.sortError: Could not save the default order

sortHint.none: Not in the default order - click to order ascending

resourceConstraints.messageDescription: What a user reads under the field when a write breaks it. Empty: PostgreSQL's own.
resourceConstraints.title: Constraints
resourceConstraints.intro: Enforced by PostgreSQL for every writer - unlike a role's Payload check (Roles), this applies no matter how the table is reached, SQL Console and external scripts included.
resourceConstraints.empty: No check constraints on this table
resourceConstraints.deleteDescription: This permanently drops `{name}`. This cannot be undone.
resourceConstraints.expressionDescription: Raw SQL boolean expression, written by hand - or build it from your columns above. For example: price > 0
resourceConstraints.errorMessageDescription: Shown instead of PostgreSQL's own generic message when this check fails. Optional - stored as the constraint's real COMMENT, so it stays attached to it even outside TotalBase. For example: Price must be greater than zero
resourceConstraints.builtConditionsDescription: Sent as they are - PostgreSQL gets the expression TotalBase writes from them, AND-joined. Remove them all to write the expression by hand instead.

resourceDataViews.title: DataViews
resourceDataViews.empty: No DataViews use this resource yet
resourceDataViews.deleteBody: This permanently deletes {name}. The underlying PostgreSQL resource is not deleted.

resourceIdempotencyKey.title: Require an idempotency key
resourceIdempotencyKey.description: {operation} without an {header} header is refused (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED), so a retried request can never run twice.
resourceIdempotencyKey.updateError: Could not update the idempotency key requirement

resourceIndexes.title: Indexes
resourceIndexes.deleteDescription: This permanently drops `{name}`. This cannot be undone.
resourceIndexes.nameDescription: Optional - a name is generated if left empty.
resourceIndexes.whereDescription: Optional raw SQL boolean expression. For example: active = true
resourceIndexes.concurrentlyHint: Avoids locking the table for writes; runs outside the main transaction.

resourceRowPresentation.intro: How a {name} row shows wherever a foreign key points at it. Every DataView column pointing here follows, unless it sets its own.
resourceRowPresentation.showDescription: The column shown instead of the key. Default: one called name, label or title, else the first text column.
resourceRowPresentation.templateDescription: Several columns at once, e.g. {example} - instead of Show; sorted by the first. Columns: {columns}.

resourceDataGrid.valueHelp: Rows whose column contains this text.
resourceDataGrid.newRowHelp: New row: fill in the first line, each value under its column. A field left empty is stored as NULL when its column allows it; a column with a default is filled by PostgreSQL - click it to set the value yourself.
resourceDataGrid.addRowNeedsPost: Turn on POST under Endpoints to add rows.
resourceDataGrid.setDefaultColumn: Filled by PostgreSQL - click to set it yourself
resourceDataGrid.deleteBody: This permanently deletes {n} selected rows. This cannot be undone.

columnPresentationFields.labelHelp: Its title wherever it shows - a form can set its own. Empty: {name}.
columnPresentationFields.labelHelpNoName: Its title wherever it shows - a form can set its own. Empty: the column's name.
columnPresentationFields.shortLabelHelp: A list's header, where room is short (Qty.). Empty: the label.
columnPresentationFields.descriptionHelp: A note on what it holds - a form shows it under the label.
columnPresentationFields.inputHelp: What every form edits it with - a form field follows it unless it picks its own. Automatic: the rule, by its type and constraints - it says which control and why; pick another to keep it.
columnPresentationFields.helpHelp: Under its input, in every form that edits it.
columnPresentationFields.placeholderHelp: An example value, inside the empty input - e.g. {example}.
columnPresentationFields.iconHelp: In its input - a unit at its end, like %.
columnPresentationFields.linkHelp: Shows the value as a link to open it.
columnPresentationFields.emptyTextHelp: Shown when it has no value. Empty: —
columnPresentationFields.optionsHelp: How each value its CHECK allows shows - its text, color and icon. Empty: the value itself.

inputReason.file: a foreign key to the files
inputReason.small-range: a whole number in a CHECK range of up to 100
inputReason.number: a number without a small range

columnPresentationSlideover.description: {dataType} - how it reads wherever it shows. What values are valid stays the database's.
columnPresentationSlideover.inherits: From its table: {keys}. An option set here replaces only that option.

resourcePage.loadErrorHelp: It may have been dropped, renamed, or is not supported here.

resourceDataPage.getOffTitle: GET is turned off for this resource
resourceDataPage.loadErrorHelp: It may have been dropped or renamed.

resourcesIndex.title: Select a database resource
resourcesIndex.description: Choose a table, view or function from the sidebar.

addColumn.title: Add column
addColumn.typeStepDescription: Pick the control that edits it - it decides the PostgreSQL column.
addColumn.searchDescription: Filter column types by name or description. Enter picks the first match.
addColumn.noMatchDescription: Nothing matches “{term}” by name or description.
addColumn.generatedFromDescription: When a row is saved with this column empty, it gets the slug of this column - for example “Mi primer artículo” becomes mi-primer-articulo. Unique: -2, -3… is added when taken.
addColumn.defaultDescription: Required if Not null is on and the table already has rows. For example: {examples}
addColumn.optionsHelp: Each option: the stored value, then the label shown for it.
addColumn.invalidTargetDescription: The target column must be a PRIMARY KEY or have a UNIQUE constraint.
addColumn.numberTypeHelp: How PostgreSQL stores it - a whole number, a big one, a fixed or a floating decimal.

resourceSuggestPresentation.title: Suggest presentation
resourceSuggestPresentation.description: What each column's type and constraints suggest - never its name. What a column lacks is ticked; a change of a value it has is not.
resourceSuggestPresentation.noneDescription: Every column already shows what its type and constraints suggest.

reasons.unique-integer: A unique whole number - a code, no thousands separator
reasons.check-pattern-code: Its CHECK pattern is digits and separators
reasons.email-pattern: Its CHECK pattern is an email address
reasons.url-pattern: Its CHECK pattern is a URL
reasons.check-list: Its CHECK list, each value as its label
reasons.unique-text: Its first unique, required text column

resourceSuggestPresentation.schemaDescription: What each table's and view's types and constraints would fill where it's missing - a change of a value it has is reviewed table by table, in its Columns.

columnConditions.intro: How it looks when something holds - the first that holds wins, per cell and per row (a cell's over a row's), on top of its style. PostgreSQL decides.
columnConditions.name: Name
columnConditions.whenHelp: A filter, as a where: other columns ($ROW.total), the user ($USER.id), dates ($CURRENT_DATE, $PERIOD), related columns.
columnConditions.needsFilter: Add at least one condition - what it checks.

columnPresentationPreview.heading: Preview
columnPresentationPreview.failed: The preview could not be read - check the conditions.

columnUsage.shownIn: Shown in {n} DataView: {names}. | Changes in {n} DataViews: {names}.

columnPresentationSummary.intro: How the column reads wherever it shows - set once, on its table.

text.label: Text
text.description: A line of text - a name, a title, a short label.

long-text.label: Text (long)
long-text.description: Several lines of plain text - a description, a note.

email.label: Email
email.description: An email address - its field offers the email keyboard; PostgreSQL checks its shape.

url.label: URL
url.description: A web address - its field offers the URL keyboard; PostgreSQL checks it starts with http(s).

phone.label: Phone
phone.description: A phone number - its field offers the phone keypad.

password.label: Password
password.description: Stored hashed - never returned by the API.

uid.label: UID
uid.description: A unique slug generated from another column.

pin.label: PIN / fixed-length code
pin.description: A short code with a fixed number of characters.

color.label: Color picker
color.description: A color, stored as a hex string.

scanner.label: Scanned code
scanner.description: Typed, or read with the device's camera - a barcode, a QR, a document's code.

html.label: Rich text (HTML)
html.description: Real HTML markup, like a mailing body.

number-field.label: Number field
number-field.description: Typed freely - an amount, a price, a percentage.

number-stepper.label: Number with − and +
number-stepper.description: Steps through whole numbers - a quantity, a count.

slider.label: Slider
slider.description: A number picked along a bounded range.

rating.label: Rating
rating.description: A star rating out of a fixed maximum.

choice.label: Choice
choice.description: One value of a fixed list, from a select.

choice-radio.label: Choice (buttons)
choice-radio.description: One value of a fixed list, each in sight.

choice-search.label: Choice (searchable)
choice-search.description: One value of a long fixed list, typed to find it.

choice-multiple.label: Choice (multiple)
choice-multiple.description: Any number of values of a fixed list.

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: A free list of short text values.

date.label: Date
date.description: A calendar date, no time of day.

datetime.label: Date and time
datetime.description: A moment - shown and picked in the viewer's time zone.

time.label: Time
time.description: A time of day, no date.

range.label: Range
range.description: From and To - a period, a span of numbers (a PostgreSQL range).

location.label: Location
location.description: The device's position, no map - where a record was made.

relation-search.label: Relation (searchable)
relation-search.description: A row of another table, typed to find it.

relation-select.label: Relation
relation-select.description: A row of another table, from a select - for a short table.

file.label: File
file.description: A single uploaded file or image.

signature.label: Signature
signature.description: Drawn by hand, saved as an image.

quickDataView.title: Create DataView
quickDataView.description: A table of its rows in the App - every column, searching, sorting and its record form. Change anything later in its settings.
quickDataView.name: Name
quickDataView.rolesHelp: Administrators always do. Opening it grants no data: each role still needs permissions on the table.
quickDataView.publishHelp: It appears in the App for these roles at once.
